changes.find: there showed a drowsy colour of weariness.
changes.reason: 色 is the look showing in the eyes, and “look” keeps the plain diction without the dictionary stiffness of “colour.”
changes.replace: there was a drowsy look of weariness.

changes.find: And smiling silently, they bent all their eyes upon the child.
changes.reason: すべてにかかる is “everything about the child,” not “all their eyes”; the gaze is poured into everything about her.
changes.replace: And smiling silently, they poured their gaze into everything about the child.

changes.find: “You won't listen, will you.”
changes.reason: きかない奴だな is rough-edged and warm, and “rascal” restores that fond roughness without dialect costume.
changes.replace: “You never listen, you rascal.”

changes.find: watched the child, never still for an instant, lovely as a small bird.
changes.reason: The “and” reattaches “lovely as a small bird” to the child she is watching, as 様子 requires.
changes.replace: watched the child, never still for an instant and lovely as a small bird.

changes.find: And holding back the smile the child helplessly brought welling up, he steadied the child
changes.reason: “made well up in him” makes the English construe while keeping the smile, the child as its cause, and the physical steadying unchanged.
changes.replace: And holding back the smile the child helplessly made well up in him, he steadied the child

changes.find: In the gaps, hastily opening his own large mouth, he pushed rice into it.
changes.reason: The Japanese repeats 彼は…彼は around his snatched mouthful, and restoring the repetition restores the rhythm of feeding himself in the gaps.
changes.replace: In the gaps, he hastily opened his large mouth, he pushed rice into his own mouth.

changes.find: far-removed heart
changes.reason: 遠くはなれた belongs to the text’s repeated far / far-off network, which “far-removed” breaks.
changes.replace: far-off heart

changes.find: she quietly remembered the quiet days filled with tears
changes.reason: 静かに is the manner of her remembering, not a quality of the days; the added second “quiet” expands the Japanese.
changes.replace: she quietly remembered the days filled with tears

changes.find: and each of the days grieved and suffered through illness.
changes.reason: In English the days cannot grieve; “days of grieving and suffering” keeps the same list without a grammar slip.
changes.replace: and each of the days of grieving and suffering through illness.

changes.find: It was in a pale dim light, and three people, quiet like the light itself, drawn close with their heads together, telling a long story.
changes.reason: The Japanese has a complete clause of three people telling a story; this only gives the English the main verb it needs, keeping the figures indefinite.
changes.replace: In a pale dim light, three people, quiet like the light itself, drawn close with heads together, were telling a long story.

changes.find: With heads bent and eyes lowered, and there only a quiet fond remembrance and forgiveness seemed to wrap them.
changes.reason: The draft leaves a fragment; the replacement finishes the clause while keeping the fixed pair “fond remembrance and forgiveness” exact.
changes.replace: With heads bent and eyes lowered, they seemed wrapped only in a quiet fond remembrance and forgiveness.

changes.find: The distant picture lay dark and quiet in the bottom of her eyes.
changes.reason: 映ってゐた is “was reflected,” the picture seen within her; “lay” loses that seeing.
changes.replace: The distant picture was reflected dark and quiet in the bottom of her eyes.

changes.find: “Why are you so quiet?”
changes.reason: He asks about 黙ってる, her not speaking, not about 静か; using “silent” keeps the silence network distinct from the quiet network.
changes.replace: “Why are you silent?”

changes.find: What is the suffering and sadness of each day. What is the weariness and trouble of each day.
changes.reason: なんだらう is wondering question, not flat statement; the question marks keep that wonder open.
changes.replace: What are the suffering and sadness of each day? What are the weariness and trouble of each day?

changes.find: Before she knew it she held a smile.
changes.reason: 微笑を浮べてゐた is a state of smiling that has come on her before she knew it; “was smiling” keeps the drift without the unidiomatic “held.”
changes.replace: Before she knew it she was smiling.

changes.find: “Why are you so quiet?” the man said again.
changes.reason: The second asking repeats the first question about her not speaking, and both must stay the same English.
changes.replace: “Why are you silent?” the man said again.

changes.find: “Truly,” she lowered her eyes again and tried to look at that picture.
changes.reason: Lowering her eyes cannot tag speech in English; a full stop keeps her words and the return to the picture separate, as the Japanese full stop does.
changes.replace: “Truly.” She lowered her eyes again and tried to look at that picture.

changes.find: She at once cried gladly in a loud voice, “Baby.”
changes.reason: After the sentence about the man, “The mother” prevents a needless reread; 彼女 here is unambiguously the mother answering with the call.
changes.replace: The mother at once cried gladly in a loud voice, “Baby.”

changes.find: and banged the spoon down upon the table: “Uma, uma, uma, uma.”
changes.reason: 『うま…』と…たゝきつけた is crying while banging, not speech after a bang; the comma and “crying” restore the simultaneity.
changes.replace: and banged the spoon down upon the table, crying “uma, uma, uma, uma.”

changes.find: All about had fallen quiet.
changes.reason: “All around” is the modern plain equivalent for あたり here and keeps “quiet” in the evening’s quiet network.
changes.replace: All around had fallen quiet.

changes.find: “It is a storm.”
changes.reason: 嵐だな is a bare weather-whisper echoing p1; the full “It is” sentence expands and lifts the last line, which must be allowed to be only a storm, isn’t it.
changes.replace: “A storm, isn’t it.”

declined.reason: “fixed all their eyes upon” keeps the draft’s wrong scope; the Japanese pours the gaze into everything about the child, so F1’s correction is taken instead.
The long p7 sentence has one clear subject, the young father, throughout; splitting it would rationalise a Japanese sentence-shape that the reading allows to run long.
うつむいて keeps the heart doing what her bowed head does at the table; “sank” tidies a deliberate bodily strangeness into a familiar feeling-word.

“indifferent, cold nastiness” still personifies the potato and strengthens 不味さ into nastiness; かゝはりのない is the potato’s cold unrelatedness, which “unconcerned” at least does not improve on, so the wording stands pending no better plain equivalent.
No replacement is offered and any clearer one would locate the vision; 前にある is kept literally because the reading forbids explaining where that rest is.
“deep in her eyes” smooths away 眼の底 and the reflected picture F6 restores; the slight strangeness of “bottom of her eyes” is the text’s spatialising of the far future.
一口には is precisely “in one breath / at one go,” the thing she cannot manage, and その眼が遠く走って belongs to the far network; “gaze drifted” would soften both into signposted drift.
小さな乳首 is physically exact and the reading keeps the nursing as physical as the feeding; “bared her breast” euphemises what the Japanese names plainly.
The Japanese gives the words in 『』 but names no speaker; adding a tag would settle who speaks the resolve, which the text leaves soft.
The Japanese as set here does give the p36 words in 『』, so the quotation marks add nothing; what it withholds is only the speaker, and that softness is preserved by keeping the quotes and no tag.

disagreements.choice: F1: the English is taken; R1 declined.
disagreements.faithful_side: F1: “all” belongs to everything about the child into which their gaze is poured, not to the parents’ eyes.
disagreements.readable_side: R1: “bent all their eyes upon” is unidiomatic and should be “fixed all their eyes upon.”

disagreements.choice: F3 for the repeated “he… he” and “In the gaps”; R5 only for the smile clause, its “In between” not taken.
disagreements.faithful_side: F3: restore the repeated 彼は…彼は and the snatched rhythm of his own mouthful.
disagreements.readable_side: R5: the smile clause is tangled and “In the gaps” should become “In between.”

disagreements.choice: The draft’s “unconcerned” and “badness” stand; only F4’s “far-off” is changed.
disagreements.faithful_side: F4: only the far network is certainly broken here; “unconcerned” is doubtful but a separate question.
disagreements.readable_side: R7: “unconcerned, cold badness” is not usable English; use “indifferent, cold nastiness.”

disagreements.choice: F6: “was reflected … in the bottom of her eyes” is taken; R12 declined.
disagreements.faithful_side: F6: 映ってゐた is the picture reflected and seen within her, in the bottom of her eyes.
disagreements.readable_side: R12: “bottom of her eyes” is not natural English; use “deep in her eyes.”

disagreements.choice: F10’s simultaneity and lower-case crying are taken; whether the babble should be “uma” at all, rather than an English yummy-noise, goes up.
disagreements.faithful_side: F10: the child cries the babble while banging the spoon; transcription style is for the editor.
disagreements.readable_side: The style sheet leaves uma-uma transcription versus plain yummy-yummy babble to an editor decision, and the translator is unsure.

disagreements.choice: Neither: the quotation marks stay and no speaker tag is added.
disagreements.faithful_side: F11: quotation marks firm an unattributed Japanese utterance into direct speech and should be removed.
disagreements.readable_side: R18: with no tag the English reader cannot tell who speaks the resolve.

data.say: House log: The desk restored the silence, far, smile and fond-remembrance/forgiveness repetitions against smoothing, accepted only grammar-level repairs elsewhere, and sent up just the baby-babble transcription.
